name: TK-HD
description: TK-HD is a closed-set benchmark for disambiguating Sino-Korean homographs in news written in three varieties: the DPRK daily Rodong Sinmun (cx), the ROK daily JoongAng Ilbo (hg), and Yanbian Daily (zg). A Sino-Korean word is a Korean lexeme of Chinese origin. Contemporary newspapers write it in hangul, and one hangul spelling can correspond to more than one hanja. Each item asks which of two train-attested hanja is the intended writing of a hangul span. The label answer_hanja is a Stage-1 automatic hangul–hanja alignment. The source is a balanced sample of 17,625 articles, 5,875 from each outlet, dated from 2006 through August 2026. Articles are split at article level (seed 42; 70/15/15), so no article appears in more than one split. The released counts are: train 12,337 articles and 487,598 items; validation 2,642 articles and 100,895 items; test 2,646 articles and 101,266 items. Every test item is binary. Of the test items, 12,970 form an anti-majority diagnostic: the hanja that is the training majority for that hangul spelling is different from the Stage-1 label. That slice is defined from the training inventory and the test labels; it is not stored as a separate file. This record contains the derived annotation layer only. TK-HD/ holds three JSONL files and manifest.json. Each line has the hangul span, two closed hanja options, the Stage-1 answer, variety, news category, article id, split, and diagnostic flags.
